Good Richmond VA web design starts with what a Richmond customer is trying to do. Someone planning a Saturday wants to know which taproom has live music and whether the kitchen is open. Someone who loved a cider at a friend's dinner wants to know which store carries it. Someone walking West Cary Street wants to know if the shop is open on Monday. Small producers and independent shops win or lose on those answers, and most of them are easier to give on a website than in an Instagram story that vanishes in a day.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, who writes and builds every page by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas. You see a free demo first, and the price is printed and paid once.

From biscuit factory to beverage district

Scott's Addition is the clearest picture of the Richmond maker economy. Planned as a residential neighborhood, it was zoned for industry under the city's first zoning ordinance in 1927. A Nabisco factory and a Chevrolet parts depot were among the early industrial tenants, and a Coca-Cola bottling plant came later. Much of that industry eventually moved out, the buildings aged, and the turnaround came through historic district status and tax credits for rehabilitating old structures.

A distillery got there first, and the first craft brewery opened in October 2013. In the mid-2010s a cidery made its home in a 1940 granite complex that once held the city's stables. Today locals call the area the Scott's Addition Beverage District, with breweries, cideries and a distillery sharing blocks with remaining industrial tenants. Every one of those producers depends on visitors who looked them up first.

Web design in Richmond for small producers

A brewery, cidery, roaster, candle maker or hot sauce company does not need what a national brand needs. It needs a handful of pages that answer the same questions customers ask at the bar every week.

  1. Tasting room or shop hours, front and centerIncluding the days you close, the kitchen or food truck hours if they differ, and whether kids and dogs are welcome.
  2. A where-to-buy pageThe stores, restaurants and markets that carry your product, grouped by area, so a fan can find you in Henrico or Chesterfield as easily as in the city.
  3. An events calendar that stays currentRelease days, live music, trivia and private bookings, with past events taken down so nobody shows up for last month's party.
  4. A wholesale and private events inquiry formA short form that sends a bar manager or a wedding planner straight to your inbox with the details you need.

What it usually does not need is a giant online store. If you sell a few items for pickup or ship merchandise, that can be added later. Start with the pages that answer the questions.

Carytown and the independent shop

Carytown is one stretch of West Cary Street, about nine blocks from the Powhite Parkway to the Boulevard, nicknamed the "Mile of Style." It holds more than 230 shops, restaurants and offices, plus the Byrd Theatre, which has shown movies since 1928. One travel guide notes many shops close or shorten hours on Mondays and that street parking fills up on weekends.

Those two details are exactly what a shop website should answer. A customer driving in from Midlothian does not want to find a locked door. The site should give the hours by day, mention where people usually park, describe what you carry in plain words, and show a few honest photos. That is a five-page Starter site, not a big project.

Jackson Ward and a long history of Black-owned business

Jackson Ward was the center of Black business life in Richmond. Maggie L. Walker chartered the St. Luke Penny Savings Bank there in 1903 and became its first president, the first African American woman to charter a bank in the United States. The bank later merged with two other Black-owned banks to form Consolidated Bank and Trust. Her home is now a National Historic Site.

Dominion Web Design Pro is a Black-owned business. That is not a reason to hire anyone on its own, but if it matters to you, it is true, and Maurice is the owner and the person who builds your site. We hold no minority business certification and do not claim one.

Richmond website design for customers who never say "Richmond"

Richmond is an independent city that belongs to no county, with Henrico County and Chesterfield County wrapped around it. Short Pump, the busy retail area west of the city, is in Henrico. Midlothian is an unincorporated community in Chesterfield. Inside the city, Manchester on the south bank of the James was its own city until it merged with Richmond in 1910, and Church Hill, the Fan and Jackson Ward each have their own pull.

Google ranks local results on relevance, distance and prominence. A customer in Midlothian searching for a gym or a photographer gets results near Midlothian. If your site never names the places you actually serve, you are leaving that to chance. A Richmond web design job done right says where you are, which nearby communities you serve, and why someone would drive over.

Which package fits a taproom, a maker or a shop

Most quotes for web design in Richmond, VA arrive after a meeting. Ours do not need one. Starter, $497 one time, covers five hand-written pages and suits a single shop or tasting room. Pro, $997, adds a 10-page site with a gallery, local SEO and Google Business Profile setup, ten researched city pages, your Google reviews on the site and an AI chat widget that is free for 14 days and then $297 a month if you keep it. Agency, $1,997, adds keyword research across your area, a page for each town and service worth having, custom design, and AI phone agent setup; that agent is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep an AI agent, or $49 a month without one. Starter goes live in 7 to 14 days. Full details are on the pricing page.

Richmond-area help before you hire anyone

  • Capital Region Small Business Development Center. Reopened in late 2020 as part of the Virginia SBDC network, it advises small businesses in the City of Richmond, the Town of Ashland and the surrounding counties. It succeeded the Greater Richmond SBDC that ChamberRVA ran from 1998 to 2018.
  • SCORE Richmond. Free mentoring for the life of your business across Richmond, Petersburg and much of Central Virginia, plus workshops for a modest fee.
  • ChamberRVA. The regional chamber, founded in 1867, covering the city and nearby counties.
  • City of Richmond Office of Community Wealth Building. Launched in 2014 and made a permanent city office in 2015, it works to raise residents' quality of life and widen their pathways to prosperity.

Common questions

How much does Richmond VA web design cost for a small business?

Local quotes vary widely and many only arrive after a discovery call. Ours are printed: $497 for the five-page Starter, $997 for Pro and $1,997 for Agency, each paid one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent. A taproom or maker usually fits Starter or Pro; Agency is for businesses that want a page for many towns and services.

Does a brewery or cidery need an online store?

Usually not a big one. Most small producers sell across the bar, at events and through stores and restaurants that carry them. What the site needs is current tasting room hours, an events calendar, a where-to-buy list and a clear way to ask about distribution or private events. If you do ship or sell for pickup, that can be added, but we will not build a large store you will not use.

Is a web design company in Richmond VA better than a remote designer?

It depends on what you want. A Richmond company can meet you in person and may already know your neighborhood. A remote designer works by phone, email and shared links, which is how most site projects run anyway. Dominion Web Design Pro is remote, one person in East Texas, and the free demo lets you judge the work before deciding.

My shop is in Short Pump. Should my site say Richmond?

Say both, honestly. Short Pump is in Henrico County, not the City of Richmond, and many customers search the community name they live in. Your contact page should give your real address and name the area, and your service or about page can say you serve the wider Richmond region.

Can you add an events calendar my staff can update?

Yes. Live music nights, trivia, release days and pop-up markets go on a simple events page. Your staff sends the changes and we update the page as part of maintenance, so the calendar never shows last month's events.
